Subject: Capacity ask ahead of renewal - Q3/Q4 outlook

Hi Monica / Rafael,

We're starting our renewal planning for the Dedicated cluster with you and wanted to share updated traffic expectations. After the last quarter's feature launch our real-time summarization endpoint has ~2.8x traffic growth and we expect sustained growth into Q4. Attached is a short worksheet with daily QPS and average token lengths projected through end of year.

High level: baseline QPS now 320 -> projected 900 by 2026-12; average tokens/request up from 350 to 420. We'll need guidance on how many reserved GPUs we should commit to and whether we can get throughput guarantees during the renewal term. Also need to understand options for burst capacity when new customers launch.

Can you propose a commitment plan and cost delta for 12 vs 24 month terms? Procurement will want an itemized view.

Thanks,
Tom
Head of Platform
SilverCrest AI

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Capacity ask ahead of renewal - Q3/Q4 outlook

Tom / Monica — reviewed the forecast. I ran the numbers assuming Redwood's M60-equivalent throughput for your model family (causal LLM, 8k context, 16-bit). Key assumptions: 64 tokens/sec per A100-80GB-equivalent for your request mix when serving with our batching and KV prefix caching. With your projected December 2026 baseline of 900 QPS and avg 420 tokens, the steady-state token/sec is ~378k tokens/sec.

Sizing options (reserved GPUs):
- Option A (conservative): 14 x A100-equivalent reserved GPUs. Handles baseline with 10% headroom; supports limited bursts via shared burst pool (up to +40% sustained for 30mins) at premium.
- Option B (balanced): 18 x A100-equivalent reserved GPUs. Target for 99.9% of steady-state demand with room for predictable week-of-month growth and smaller launches. Includes 10% monthly usage credits for burst capacity and automatic slot-shifting to match peak windows.
- Option C (aggressive / 24-month discount): 22 x A100-equivalent reserved GPUs. Designed for <1% throttling risk during sustained growth and includes an SLO: 95th-percentile token latency under your current 600ms tail for production routes; guaranteed incident credits for SLA breach.

Estimated committed monthly cost (list pricing before negotiations):
- 12m Option A: $135k/month
- 12m Option B: $172k/month
- 24m Option C: $290k/month (reflects volume discount)

Notes and tradeoffs:
- We can include a peak-burst feature that buys time-limited extra capacity (charged on top of committed) for launches.
- For token-heavy bursts we recommend enabling prefix KV caching on your most common prompts — that reduces per-token compute by ~18% in our benchmarks. Karthik can help with config.
- Pricing above is for reserved A100-equivalent capacity; we can propose a mixed cluster with some lower-cost T4/RTX-8 options for non-critical batch workloads to reduce cost.

I'll attach a short SLA draft and the cost worksheet. Happy to walk the team through the math on a call.

Regards,
Rafael Mendes
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks Rafael — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. Two follow-ups from our side:
1) Procurement will push for a 24-month commitment if the unit pricing for Option C can be lowered ~8-12% from the draft. Can Redwood entertain a ~10% deeper discount if we commit to a minimum monthly usage floor and allow an annual true-up?
2) For the SLA: can you clarify what constitutes an SLA incident (service-wide vs. per-route) and the credit ladder? We prefer credits applied monthly to committed spend rather than one-off credit notes.

Also, any chance to carve out a lower-cost dev pool (non-production) that we can pin to a separate billing code? That would help our engineering teams run nightly jobs without hitting prod capacity.

Nora
Head of Ops, SilverCrest AI
